scenarios.theme: The executor maximum is 100 but only ten workers run. Why is the queue growing?
scenarios.assumptions: A Java 21 executor has corePoolSize ten, maximumPoolSize one hundred and an unbounded queue. Traffic queues for seconds. What will you change and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

scenarios.theme: Four running parents wait for four queued children. Add four threads?

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Thread Pools to nested task deadlock.

scenarios.assumptions: A dispatcher submits expensive tasks to a saturated executor and the rejection policy runs them inline. Other connections stop progressing. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Keep that dispatcher free of expensive blocking/CPU work

scenarios.theme: Callers time out but queued tasks later execute writes. How do you stop stale work?
scenarios.assumptions: A backlog outlives request deadlines. When workers become free, they perform operations whose callers already retried. What will you change?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Thread Pools to cancelled queue.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Callers time out but queued tasks later execute writes. How do you stop stale work?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Carry operation identity and deadline with each task; reject expired queued work before execution where semantics allow, support documented cancellation an

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Removing queued work cannot undo an active side effect

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Shorten queues and admission so most accepted work can meet its objective.
